doc: Triple Screen (Alexander Elder, Trading for a Living, Wiley 1993). Screen one finds the tide on the longer time frame (weekly) by the slope of a 13-period EMA and of the MACD (12, 26, 9) histogram: trade only with it. Screen two, the wave, uses an oscillator against the tide on the shorter frame (daily): the 2-period EMA of force index (price change times volume) below zero in an uptide is a buy zone. Screen three is a trailing buy-stop above the prior bar's high (not drawn). This preset is the shorter frame: EMA 13 and 26, MACD histogram and force index(2) panes, and Elder's impulse system as a strip of dots (Come Into My Trading Room, Wiley 2002): green when both the EMA 13 and the MACD histogram rise, red when both fall, blue otherwise; green bars forbid selling, red forbid buying. Screen one needs weekly bars: supply them to compose the same preset on the longer frame.
